name: Automatically install expanded theory without losing existing lines
covers: Italian Giuoco Piano, Pianissimo, Two Knights and Evans gambit
Spanish Morphy, Berlin, Exchange and Marshall variations
Sicilian Scheveningen, Classical, Sveshnikov and Taimanov
Scandinavian Qa5, Qd6 and modern lines
description: Verifies the expanded theory pack is added once to existing repertoires and preserves user-created lines.
steps: Open RepertoireLab with the previous repertoire already saved
Wait for the expanded theory to appear
Search for Italian Giuoco Piano, Spanish Berlin, Scotch gambit, Sicilian Scheveningen, Scandinavian Qa5, Benoni and Petroff
Refresh the page
expected: The new opening branches are present after migration, survive refresh without duplication, and existing custom lines remain.

name: Explore a position and follow candidate opening moves
covers: rank moves by side-to-move win/draw statistics
combine database score with live local Stockfish WebAssembly analysis
run local Stockfish independently of cached cloud evaluations
fallback to database score when local engine cannot start
save a new branch from the current board
update an existing line from the current board
description: Verifies the board-driven repertoire tree supports jumping to a move, saving a new branch, and updating the selected line.
steps: Open Mijn repertoire and expand the repertoire tree
Click a move inside a saved line to load that position
Click Aanbevelingen op winrate + engine
Inspect move win/draw statistics and available engine scores
Choose a suggested move and play it on the board
Enter a branch name and click Vertakking opslaan
Inspect the repertoire list and refresh the page
expected: The new branch appears as a saved repertoire line and remains after refresh; the move suggestions are ranked using the side-to-move database score and a fresh local Stockfish 19 Lite WebAssembly analysis, with a database-only fallback if the local engine fails.

name: Check repertoire depth against the master database
description: Verifies users can set a target for final-position frequency and check stored lines against the Lichess master database.
steps: Open Mijn repertoire
Set a maximum master-game target
Click Controleer openingsdiepte
Inspect status for checked lines
expected: Each checked line shows whether its final position is below the target, needs extension, or could not be checked.

name: Study the expanded repertoire on mobile
description: Verifies expanded theory remains searchable and usable on a narrow screen.
steps: Open Mijn repertoire on mobile
Search for Najdorf
Open a matching line
Inspect the board, moves, and strategic notes
expected: Search finds the prepared lines and a selected line can be studied on the interactive board with its notes.

name: Reject invalid custom opening notation
description: Verifies invalid notation is rejected without adding a broken opening line.
steps: Choose Nieuwe variant
Enter a name and invalid PGN such as 1. e4 Zz9
Submit the form
Inspect the repertoire list
expected: A visible notation error appears and the invalid line is not added.

name: Autofill repertoire and inspect Lichess games
description: Verifies users can select a rating group, add popular continuations from the current position, and review recent public games against saved repertoire lines.
steps: Open Mijn repertoire and select the rating group around 1800
Load a position with known opening moves on the board
Click Vul repertoire automatisch aan vanuit deze stelling
Verify suggested branches appear in the repertoire list
Enter a valid public Lichess username and click Controleer partijen
Inspect the game-by-game repertoire match report
expected: New branches are saved without duplicating existing lines, and the game review displays a match or deviation summary for available public games.
